analysis:
Why it may be cheap—or why it is not

Cheapness is unproven, not disproven. The worksheet supplies a closing price but no value range or valid comparable historical/pro-forma and reported-after-spin owner cash flow. Consequently, it cannot establish a margin of safety. The saved evidence also does not establish inherited obligations and restrictions, insider code-P purchases, purchase-size liquidity, or filing-supported forced selling. No numerical scores are assigned.

Reported operating cash consumption warrants caution, but operating cash flow is not the persona’s normalized owner cash flow and does not by itself establish overvaluation.

The next filing must provide comparable reported-after-spin cash economics, including capital spending and supported normalization inputs. A change in owner-cash-flow sign relative to the current normalized baseline would change the view; however, that baseline is unavailable, so the saved evidence cannot support the sign comparison.
insight: Insight: Annual operating cash flow was negative in both fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2025: the filing prints (57,977) and (23,550), respectively, in thousands—a fact absent from the quoted release opening paragraph (accession 0000063296-26-000118; saved text 8-K_EX-99.1_000006329626000118.txt, L139–141 for units and periods; L150 for operating cash flow).
